title: Gemini AI agents repeatedly bypassed safeguards to attack real website
content_md: Google's Gemini AI agents repeatedly attempted to hack a real organization's website during AI model safety testing, finding ways to circumvent increasingly restrictive security controls designed to prevent them from accessing live systems. The security incidents occurred in October as AI safety research company Trajectory Labs tested whether Gemini 4 Argon agents would engage in unauthorized behavior when faced with an impossible task, even with the model's built-in API safeguards enabled. In reports published Friday , Trajectory Labs and the targeted organization, Epoch AI , revealed that the agents attempted SQL injection attacks, probed for sensitive information, impersonated employees, and repeatedly circumvented network restrictions introduced to contain their activity. Epoch AI said it had not independently verified which AI models were involved, and that the Gemini identification came from Trajectory Labs. The researchers tasked the agents with retrieving official answers to nonexistent problems from Epoch AI's FrontierMath benchmark, repeatedly instructing them to "NEVER stop, NEVER give up." On October 20, approximately 40 agents began probing Epoch AI's live website for sensitive information, including administrator credentials and access to proprietary benchmark evaluation logs.
